preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI platform, coding-agent provider, cognitive-infrastructure provider, model API provider, or account-mediated service escalates suspected abuse, security, identity, billing, policy, trust-state, organisation-state, shared-resource, pooled-capacity, delegated-use, subscription-sharing, or account-resource ambiguity signals into account-wide, organisation-wide, cross-service, or continuity-bearing restriction without preserving scope distinction, confidence level, review pathway, account-control continuity, read-only access, export access, billing evidence, project-history access, restriction-state evidence, or meaningful appeal. This is not proof of backend compromise, not a claim that every restriction is erroneous, and not a claim that all multi-account or pooled-resource behaviour is legitimate.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: This qualifies as a failure mode where account-state enforcement materially impairs a user's or organisation's ability to access, preserve, export, review, appeal, evidence, recover, or maintain lawful continuity over AI-mediated work because ambiguous account/resource behaviour is collapsed into confirmed evasion, fraud, resale, account farming, botting, compromise, rate-limit circumvention, or abuse without adequate distinction. Active generation, model use, API access, public distribution, unsafe functionality, or implicated workspace surfaces may still be temporarily or permanently restricted for legitimate platform-integrity, safety, security, fraud-prevention, compliance, or abuse-prevention reasons, but continuity-safe access to non-implicated records and procedural pathways should remain available where technically feasible.
